Formulation  
Predisposing: Chronic illness (SLE) requiring immunosuppressive therapy may heighten health vigilance.  
Precipitating: Acute onset of chest pain, hemoptysis, and fever triggered fear of serious disease.  
Perpetuating: Uncertainty pending further medical assessment.  
Protective: Prompt help-seeking behaviour; ability to articulate concerns.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety about current physical illness.  
- Patient Goal(s): “Know whether I’m dying of lung cancer”; reduce worry once diagnosis clarified.  
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide clear medical information; monitor anxiety; facilitate coping while investigations proceed.  
- Actions (Patient): Attend same-day face-to-face GP review; follow through with any investigations; use provided information to manage worry.  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange urgent in-person assessment; explain likely diagnosis (chest infection) vs. cancer; offer reassurance; consider brief psycho-education on health anxiety at follow-up.  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded.  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Likely chest infection vs. lung cancer; need for physical examination; possible antibiotics; prognosis.  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased health anxiety if symptoms persist or new alarming symptoms arise.  
- Coping Strategies: Seek timely medical review; avoid catastrophic interpretations until results available; maintain routine daily activities as tolerated.
